name: Benralizumab
route_note: Subcutaneous injection every 4 weeks for the first three doses, then every 8 weeks

discovery.note: Humanised afucosylated IgG1κ antibody against IL-5Rα made with BioWa's Potelligent technology, enhancing ADCC.

tagline: Afucosylated IL-5 receptor antibody that depletes eosinophils, dosed every 8 weeks
summary: Benralizumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody against the IL-5 receptor α chain that rapidly and almost completely depletes eosinophils. It is used for severe eosinophilic asthma and, since 2024, eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
mechanism: Benralizumab binds IL-5Rα, expressed on eosinophils and basophils, blocking IL-5 signalling.
Its afucosylated Fc binds FcγRIIIa on natural killer cells with high affinity, triggering antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity that eliminates eosinophils in blood and tissue within 24 hours.
uses: Severe eosinophilic asthma (adults and children ≥6 years)

history.title: SIROCCO and CALIMA
history.detail: Phase 3 trials show reduced exacerbations in eosinophilic asthma.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in November for severe eosinophilic asthma.

history.title: EU and Japan approval
history.detail: Approved in the EU and Japan in January.

history.title: COPD trials fail
history.detail: GALATHEA and TERRANOVA do not meet primary endpoints in COPD.

history.title: EGPA
history.detail: FDA approves benralizumab for EGPA (MANDARA, non-inferior to mepolizumab).

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: After loading, maintenance dosing is only once every 8 weeks.
Eosinophils in blood become nearly undetectable within a day of the first dose.
